span.label: posts and reactions from questionable outlets grow at the same pace as those from reliable ones inside a platform, so the questionable series is a re-scaling of the reliable one. THE ONLY THING THAT VARIES IS THE SCALING FACTOR, AND IT VARIES BY PLATFORM - which means a single-platform study measures its platform, not the phenomenon
span.term: the same curve, a different multiplier

span.label: Gab posts about 70% as much questionable as reliable content and reacts to it about three times more. Counting posts and counting reactions therefore rank the platforms differently, and the amplification factor exists precisely to separate them
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: reliability comes from Media Bias/Fact Check at the level of the news outlet. Every article from a listed outlet inherits its label, and every article from an unlisted one is invisible. The paper states the limit and prints the six criteria rather than citing the list, which is what makes the boundary checkable
span.term: the label is on the outlet, and the authors say so
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: every platform's data was gathered by the same Google-Trends-derived keyword list, and on Gab the hashtags were then manually browsed and selected by meaning. What is in the dataset is what those keywords caught, and the comparability across five platforms rests on the list being applied identically
span.term: the keyword set is the aperture
